WI-17 (UC-009 final web WI): Playwright e2e for the analytics feature (AC#9). Added web/e2e/analytics.spec.ts — one serial describe with two happy-path tests in the desktop chromium project (does not match the mobile-driver/mobile-customer testMatch globs; no playwright.config.ts change needed, mirrors onboarding.spec.ts).

FLOWS COVERED:
1. AC9_FleetAdminAnalytics (9.1s isolated): FleetAdmin (admin@demo.local / Demo1234! on fleet 'demo') logs in via the /x/login UI, clicks the FleetAdmin-gated 'Analytika' nav item -> /x/analytics. Asserts the Overview (Prehled) trend chart renders as a real canvas role=img ('Vyvoj jizd a trzeb') — its presence proves a non-empty series (empty-state would replace the chart) — plus the 'Jizdy' KPI label and no error state. Then switches the date-range preset to 'Poslednich 7 dni' (a today-containing preset; the chart re-renders non-empty) and switches to the Ridici (drivers) tab, which renders the visible league DataTable (caption 'Statistiky ridicu' + >=1 body row) from a successful API response, with no error state.
2. AC9_SuperAdminPlatform (3.0s isolated): SuperAdmin logs in via the /admin/login UI (#admin-email/#admin-password -> POST /auth/admin/login), then reaches the Platform screen by clicking the in-app 'Prehled platformy' link on /admin (client-side nav). Asserts the demo fleet row ('Taxi Demo Kolin'), the 'Flotila' column header, and the 'Souhrn platformy' totals region, with no error state.

DATA ANCHOR (why assertions are shaped this way): the e2e harness seeds ONLY DevelopmentSeeder (Program.cs startup), NOT the 50k ReportSeedScript (invoked directly by API integration tests only). The demo fleet's analytics signal is the handful of demo orders anchored at now(), of which DEMO05 is a Completed ride (180 CZK, driver1). That single completed ride this month guarantees a non-empty Overview series and rides>=1. Numeric assertions are kept minimal (chart present / label visible / not-error, not exact values) so a seed tweak will not break the spec. The drivers league returns a row per active fleet driver regardless of activity, and the admin/analytics endpoint lists all active fleets, so both tables are structurally guaranteed non-empty.

DEVIATION RESOLVED POSITIVELY (admin-screen reachability): the task caveat and the code comment in PlatformScreen.tsx claim the SuperAdmin screen is unreachable because the backend cannot mint a SuperAdmin JWT via any login path. This is STALE. onboarding.spec.ts already proves the A7b path: the create-superadmin CLI (execSync, idempotent) inserts a fleetless SuperAdmin, and POST /auth/admin/login (the same endpoint the /admin/login UI posts to) returns a role=SuperAdmin token. beforeAll runs ensureSuperAdmin() (idempotent — 'SuperAdmin already exists' on re-run) and the spec logs in through the real /admin/login UI. Admin e2e is ACHIEVED via UI login; the PlatformScreen.tsx 'unreachable' comment should be updated in a follow-up (out of scope for this e2e WI).

DEBUG NOTE: the SuperAdmin test initially failed on the platform-table locator. In the fix I changed TWO things at once and did NOT isolate which one mattered: (a) navigation from page.goto('/admin/platform') (full reload) to a client-side click on the '/admin' -> '/admin/platform' PlatformLink, and (b) the locator from getByRole('table', {name: /Prehled platformy/}) (matching PlatformScreen's CLIPPED SrCaption) to content-based locators (getByText('Taxi Demo Kolin') + getByRole('columnheader', {name:'Flotila'}) + the 'Souhrn platformy' region). The likely root cause is (b): authStorage.getUserRole() reads from localStorage (persisted by useAdminLogin's setTokens), so a same-origin reload should preserve the SuperAdmin role and AdminGuard should pass — so the caption-name locator against the clipped caption is the more probable culprit (test 1 succeeds against DriversTab's VISIBLE caption, the one structural difference). Both changes were kept — content-based locators + client-side nav are the more robust choice regardless. i18n strings were verified against cs.json (preset select aria-label 'Obdobi'; error text 'Nepodarilo se nacist analyticka data.'; demo fleet name 'Taxi Demo Kolin'; platform load-fail 'Prehled platformy se nepodarilo nacist.').

LIGHTHOUSE (AC#10): manual Lighthouse a11y >=90 on /x/analytics is a manual DEMO.md step per rules/web-accessibility.md#a11y-gate — not run in this automated pass; recorded here as a to-do for the DEMO notes.

SPEC RUNTIMES: isolated chromium run of analytics.spec.ts = 1.1 min total wall (harness boot ~50s + 9.1s + 3.0s tests). In the full suite the analytics file was reported as a slow file at 39.2s including its harness share.

FULL E2E TALLY (npm run --prefix web e2e, fresh run, read full output): 12 passed, 1 failed, 1 did not run. BOTH analytics tests PASSED. The single failure is a FULL-SUITE-ONLY BROWSER-SETUP FLAKE, not an assertion failure and not in my chromium spec: [mobile-driver] driver.spec.ts:162 Driver_Decline_ReturnsOrderToNew failed with 'browserContext.newPage: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded while setting up page' (a browser-context/page-setup timeout in the mobile-driver project, amid repeated SignalR 'Connection disconnected' log spam), which cascaded to skip driver.spec.ts:189 (Driver_OfflineArrive_QueuedThenDeliveredExactlyOnce = 'did not run'). DECISIVE ISOLATION EVIDENCE: running the mobile-driver project ALONE (npx playwright test --project=mobile-driver) = ALL 3 driver tests PASS, including Driver_Decline (19.2s) and Driver_OfflineArrive (10.6s). So the failure is a full-suite resource/timing issue at browser-context setup, NOT a logic defect in driver.spec and NOT an analytics-assertion problem. HONEST CAVEAT: because I added a beforeAll dotnet subprocess + 2 more browser contexts to the suite, I cannot claim my change has ZERO effect on shared full-suite timing — but the failure is a browser-setup timeout in a SEPARATE project (analytics.spec is in the chromium project) that disappears in isolation, which is the signature of harness/browser-resource flakiness rather than a defect introduced by my spec. Did NOT modify driver.spec.ts and did NOT retry-to-green. My isolated analytics-only run (2 passed) and the isolated mobile-driver run (3 passed) together confirm every spec is green in isolation.
